items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: And then something else happened to the show that hadn't happened since Russ Columbo, the matinee idol, you know.

ctx.x: So, that's why (unintelligible) with this idea. I would say, 'Well thank you, sir.' And the next thing I knew, here come the radio people. Some critics, some writer -- he used to do a column called "Broadway after dark." So, he had me like to go over the the Hilton Hotel and broadcast, you know, and interview, you know, over there. He done this twice. So, now the box offices -- I mean they're clamoring for tickets, reservations, you know, building up.
And then something else happened to the show that hadn't happened since Russ Columbo, the matinee idol, you know. The raised the box office price to twice its normal, you know, amount, see.

Then someone else come, you see. This Harry Joe Brown, Junior, and some real estate men from up from Westchester. And they had this house down there where Orson Wells used to broadcast (unintelligible) theater." See, it was the largest seating capacity. And they wanted us to represent the show in their theater, you see. And -- oh, yeah, you know, from the Capezio shoe company, you know. They come back stage and he says, you know -- invited -- gave us an invitation
